overview: San Marino is a tiny landlocked country completely surrounded by Italy. It claims to be the oldest surviving republic in the world, traditionally said to have been founded in 301. Its capital is the City of San Marino. It uses the euro, although it is not a member of the European Union.

geography.text: San Marino sits on and around Monte Titano, in the foothills of the Apennines, not far from Italy's Adriatic coast. Three medieval towers stand on the mountain's peaks, and the old town looks out over the surrounding Italian countryside.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild Mediterranean climate on the slopes of Monte Titano, with cold winters at the top.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Foxes, badgers and many birds live in the woods around the mountain.

history.text: According to tradition, San Marino was founded in 301 by Marinus, a stonemason from the island of Rab who fled the persecution of Christians. Protected by its mountain and by careful diplomacy, it has kept its independence ever since. Napoleon offered to enlarge it, but San Marino politely refused. Its constitution, dating from 1600, is one of the oldest still in force.

events.title: Founding
events.text: By tradition, Saint Marinus founds a community on Monte Titano.

events.title: Constitution
events.text: San Marino's written constitution is adopted.

events.title: Napoleon's offer
events.text: Napoleon offers more land; San Marino accepts only his friendship.

events.title: Treaty with Italy
events.text: A friendship treaty with the new Kingdom of Italy secures its independence.

events.title: Joins the UN
events.text: San Marino becomes a member of the United Nations.

government.text: San Marino has two heads of state, called Captains Regent, who are elected by parliament every six months, a tradition dating back to the 1200s. The Great and General Council, its 60-member parliament, is elected every five years. San Marino is not in the European Union but uses the euro.

economy.text: Tourism, banking and manufacturing are the main parts of San Marino's economy, which is closely tied to Italy. Its coins and stamps are prized by collectors.

culture.text: San Marino claims to be the oldest surviving republic in the world. Its three towers on top of Monte Titano appear on its flag and coat of arms, and the historic centre is a UNESCO site.

items.title: The Three Towers
items.text: Guaita, Cesta and Montale stand on the peaks of Monte Titano.

items.title: Captains Regent
items.text: Two heads of state who change every 1 April and 1 October.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Torta Tre Monti, a layered wafer cake named after the three towers.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The medieval historic centre is a UNESCO site.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On 1 April and 1 October, two new Captains Regent take office in a colourful ceremony.

sport.text: San Marino's football team is one of the weakest in the world but plays with great pride; it famously scored against England after just 8 seconds in 1993. The San Marino Grand Prix in Formula 1 was actually held in nearby Imola, Italy.

items.text: Davide Gualtieri scored after 8 seconds against England.
San Marino beat Liechtenstein 1–0, its first ever win in a competitive match.
San Marino won its first Olympic medals, in shooting and wrestling.

didYouKnow: San Marino is completely surrounded by Italy.
San Marino has more vehicles than people.

keyPeople.name: Saint Marinus
keyPeople.text: According to tradition, founded the community in 301.

keyPeople.name: Alessandra Perilli
keyPeople.text: Won San Marino's first Olympic medals, in 2021.
